stemMd: An organism obtains carbon from organic compounds and absorbs nutrients after secreting digestive enzymes into its surroundings. Which feeding strategy is described?
explanationMd: The organism relies on pre-existing organic carbon, so it is heterotrophic. Digestion occurs outside the body and soluble products are then absorbed. This is a common fungal strategy and differs from ingesting food into an internal digestive compartment.

distractorRationale.a: Photoautotrophs use light and inorganic carbon rather than absorbing digested organic material.
distractorRationale.b: This uses inorganic energy sources and inorganic carbon.
distractorRationale.d: The description explicitly places digestion outside the organism.
distractorRationale.c: Nitrogen fixation concerns conversion of atmospheric nitrogen, not this carbon-feeding strategy.
